items.title: IHC rules infringement of fundamental rights breaches Constitution ahead of PTI’s Sept 27 protest
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that any activity resulting in infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights amounts to a violation of the Constitution, warning that public office holders responsible for such violations would also be deemed to have breached their oath of office. The ruling came in a detailed 37-page judgment on a petition concerning the proposed nationwide PTI protest towards Islamabad on September 27, 2026. PTI had announced the march to demand release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. A citizen, Waqas Ahmed, had challenged the planned move on the grounds that the protest could disrupt routine life, traffic and business activities in the federal capital. A three-member bench headed by Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and comprising Justice Muhammad Asif and Justice Muhammad Azam Khan issued the judgment. The bench had announced its short order on September 14 after hearing Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan, Additional Attorney General Amir Rehman, the advocate generals of the four provinces and Islamabad, and counsel for the petitioner, Barrister Akhter Cheena. The court described the case as requiring an “unusual degree of constitutional balance” between the right of political parties and citizens to assemble peacefully and express dissent, and the rights of other citizens to life, liberty, dignity, free movement, trade, business, property, and access to hospitals, educational institutions, courts and workplaces. “The question is not whether a political party is entitled to protest. It plainly is, subject always to the Constitution and law,” the judgment observed. The court held that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the fundamental rights of other citizens. A key objection raised by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa advocate general concerned the territorial jurisdiction of the IHC over provincial authorities functioning outside Islamabad. Rejecting the objection, the court held that Article 199(1)(c) empowered a high court to issue directions where a governmental power or function was being exercised “in, or in relation to” territory within its jurisdiction. The court clarified, however, that the provision did not confer general supervisory jurisdiction over another province. A high court could issue directions to an authority outside its territorial seat where the governmental function had a direct and proximate legal relation with territory within its jurisdiction and intervention was necessary to protect fundamental rights there. The bench also observed that where executive action or inaction was likely to infringe the fundamental rights of citizens within Islamabad, the court was under a “bounden duty” to assume jurisdiction under Article 199(1)(c). The court also rejected the objection that the petition was not maintainable because KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had not been impleaded as a respondent. It noted that the Advocate General KP was representing both the provincial government and the chief minister. The court further rejected the argument that the petitioner had an adequate alternate remedy under the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act, 2024. It noted that no application had, admittedly, been filed under Section 3 of the Act and observed that its provisions had not been adhered to by the KP chief minister and others who had announced their intention to march towards Islamabad. The judgment extensively referred to the Supreme Court’s decision in the Faizabad sit-in case, observing that the constitutional right to assemble and protest was protected but remained subject to restrictions where its exercise infringed the fundamental rights of others. The IHC also referred to the Supreme Court judgment concerning the PTI march of May 25, 2022, noting that assurances regarding a peaceful rally and non-obstruction of the Srinagar Highway had not been honoured. The judgment referred to damage to public and private property, fires in the Blue Area greenbelt, injuries to police personnel and the subsequent invocation of Article 245 to call in the armed forces in aid of civil power. The court also cited its November 21, 2024 order directing that no protest, rally or sit-in be allowed in violation of the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act. It observed that the order had also been flouted. During the proceedings, the court allowed the Islamabad deputy commissioner/district magistrate to place electronic material on record. Video clips of the 2022 and 2024 protests were played before the bench, which described the conduct shown in the footage as “highly disturbing and reflective of violence and aggression”. The court noted that PTI was in power in KP during both episodes and observed that provincial government resources had been used in pursuit of political objectives. Regarding the proposed September 27 march, the court held that the petitioner’s apprehension was not merely speculative. It noted that the date and destination of the proposed gathering were known and that statements attributed to the KP chief minister indicated that the date was firm and that he intended to lead the march. While disposing of the petition, the court directed that no political party, political leader, provincial government or public office holder could lawfully occupy roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas, buildings or similar public places within, or leading to or from, Islamabad in a manner that obstructed free movement or hindered trade, business, professions or access to medical and educational facilities. The provincial governments and chief ministers were directed to ensure that no government resources, public funds, officials, vehicles, machinery or equipment were used directly or indirectly to facilitate any march, rally or procession towards Islamabad. They were also directed to ensure that no public servant was compelled, coerced or induced to participate in such activities. The chief secretaries, police chiefs, federal interior secretary, chief commissioner and IG Islamabad were ordered to issue instructions prohibiting officials from complying with orders requiring them to facilitate such marches. Officials facing coercion were directed to report the matter to the relevant authorities, while helplines or other communication mechanisms were ordered to be established for this purpose. The court further directed the authorities to take departmental action against officials who violated the directions. In a significant finding, the court held that any person whose activity resulted in a violation of the fundamental rights of citizens in Islamabad would be deemed to have violated the Constitution and would be liable for consequences under the law. It further declared that any public office holder whose activity resulted in a violation of citizens’ fundamental rights would be deemed to have violated both the Constitution and his or her oath of office.

items.title: Shakira to cap off world tour with Madrid 12-gig run
items.description: Shakira will kick off on Friday evening a marathon twelve-concert run in Madrid, bringing an end to both her world tour and the Colombian superstar’s eight-year absence from Spain. The 49-year-old “Hips Don’t Lie” and “Waka Waka (This Time For Africa)” singer will take to a temporary 50,000-seater “Shakira stadium” erected in the south of the Spanish capital up till October 11, according to events giant Live Nation. With no other European tour dates announced, Madrid’s authorities are expecting a significant economic windfall from her grand return, after welcoming fellow Hispanic superstar Bad Bunny in May and June for a series of 10 gigs. Shakira has not performed in Spain since 2018, several years before her separation from former Spanish footballing great Gerard Pique was made public in 2022. She embarked on a world tour in February 2025 to promote “Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran” (Women no longer cry), an album inspired by her breakup with the legendary Barcelona defender which won her a fourth Grammy award. Across her decades-long career, Shakira has sold more than 95 million records worldwide and performed at both the opening ceremony and final of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. “Waka Waka (This Time For Africa)” was also the official song for the 2010 tournament in South Africa, the first time world football’s premiere showcase was held on the continent. Her return to Madrid also comes after she paid a 7.3-million-euro fine ($8.4 million) in November 2023 as part of an agreement with the Spanish courts, in which she pleaded guilty to avoid having to stand trial for tax fraud. In the high-profile affair, Shakira also paid the Spanish taxman 17.45 million euros to settle her affairs in the country. items.title: One Family, Many Farewells – At Lashibi Funeral Homes
items.description: For nearly 25 years, Mrs. Olive Dovlo has relied on Lashibi Funeral Homes and Crematorium whenever her family has experienced a loss. Her relationship with Lashibi began when her uncle, her mother’s brother, passed away. The service her family received gave her the confidence to return following the deaths of her mother and other relatives. Over the years, she has also recommended Lashibi to friends and other families. “I have dealt with Lashibi for many years, from the time they started. I have taken several of my relatives there and recommended them to other people,” she says. Her trust was established during that first experience. “When we called, they responded very well. We took my uncle there, and they did a good job. That is why I kept going back.” That confidence was tested again when her cousin died about a year ago. Although the body had initially been taken to another mortuary, Mrs. Dovlo preferred to have the arrangements handled by Lashibi. “I told the family, ‘I don’t deal with other mortuaries. I only deal with Lashibi.’ I called them, and they immediately picked up the body and brought it straight to Lashibi. It was stress-free.” She says this support relieved her nephews and nieces of the burden of moving between different service providers and managing arrangements themselves. Punctuality has also been central to her experience. “Once you give them the date and time, they see to it that everything is on track,” she explains. “Whether it is a pick-up or another service, they are always punctual. “ Over the years, members of the Lashibi team have become familiar and trusted faces. She remembers Elliot, an undertaker who assisted her family, and speaks warmly of Mr. Otu, the Operations Lead, and Gina at the reception. “Gina is very good. Mr. Otu knows she is my favourite, so whenever I have something to do, he assures me Gina will handle it effortlessly.” Mrs. Dovlo also appreciates the courteous reception team, the maintenance of the cemetery and the convenience of having funeral-related services in one location, including caskets, the Chapel and reception facilities. “They have it all and I am elated with all the services provided. The cemetery is well kept, and the staff are receptive.” She values being able to return to the cemetery to visit relatives buried there. With prior notice, family members can use the designated sitting areas and spend time remembering their loved ones. As Lashibi Funeral Homes and Crematorium marks its 25th anniversary, Mrs. Dovlo’s message reflects the loyalty built over almost a quarter of a century. “Keep it up. Keep doing the good work for us. I will always come back to Lashibi.”

items.title: 126 terroristes identifiés grâce à l’Intelligence artificielle
items.description: INTERPOL a rendu public, ce vendredi 18 septembre 2026, les résultats d’une opération dénommée Shams II, menée en juin à Tunis. Grâce notamment à l’intelligence artificielle et à la reconnaissance faciale, l’opération a permis d’identifier 126 combattants terroristes étrangers présumés à partir de milliers d’images issues de contenus diffusés en ligne par des groupes jihadistes. Coordonnée par l’Organisation internationale de police criminelle, l’opération Shams II s’est déroulée du 1er au 5 juin 2026 dans la capitale tunisienne. Elle a mobilisé 28 officiers et experts spécialisés venus de 11 pays. Durant cinq jours, les enquêteurs ont extrait 108 076 images faciales de contenus visuels associés à des groupes jihadistes. Des outils d’intelligence artificielle et des scripts automatisés ont été utilisés pour accélérer la collecte, éliminer les doublons et vérifier la qualité des données. Après ce premier traitement, le corpus a été ramené à 6 362 images faciales uniques, jugées suffisamment exploitables pour être soumises au système de reconnaissance faciale d’INTERPOL. Les résultats générés par les outils automatisés ont ensuite été contrôlés et vérifiés par des officiers et analystes spécialisés, conformément aux règles de l’organisation sur le traitement des données. 126 suspects identifiés À ce stade, 126 combattants terroristes étrangers présumés ont été identifiés à partir des images analysées. Ces correspondances doivent permettre d’enrichir les renseignements déjà disponibles sur les suspects, notamment, sur leurs déplacements potentiels et leurs réseaux. Des centaines d’images supplémentaires ont également été apportées par le Bureau central national d’INTERPOL à Bagdad, en Irak, dans le cadre d’un important ensemble de données consacré aux suspects liés au terrorisme. Les nouvelles informations sont progressivement intégrées aux bases de données d’INTERPOL afin d’appuyer les efforts internationaux de détection, de suivi et de perturbation des déplacements de personnes soupçonnées de liens avec le terrorisme. Certaines pistes issues de l’opération sont déjà exploitées dans des procédures judiciaires menées dans plusieurs pays participants, dont une affaire impliquant deux suspects actuellement détenus. L’argent et la radicalisation en ligne dans le viseur Shams II ne s’est pas limitée à l’identification biométrique. Les enquêteurs ont également utilisé des outils spécialisés dans les cryptomonnaies pour tenter de retracer des financements illicites. Ces investigations ont débouché sur trois demandes urgentes adressées à un prestataire de services sur actifs virtuels afin d’obtenir des informations relatives à des clients. L’opération a, par ailleurs, ouvert un volet consacré à la radicalisation des jeunes dans les environnements numériques. Des échanges ont, notamment, eu lieu avec des représentants de l’industrie du jeu vidéo afin de renforcer la coopération et le partage d’informations sur ce phénomène. Onze pays mobilisés La Côte d’Ivoire, le Ghana, l’Irak, le Kenya, la Malaisie, le Nigeria, les Philippines, le Qatar, le Tadjikistan, la Tunisie et l’Ouzbékistan ont pris part à l’opération. Shams II a été conduite dans le cadre du projet CT TECH+, financé par les instruments de politique étrangère de l’Union européenne et soutenu par le Bureau des Nations unies de lutte contre le terrorisme (UNOCT). INTERPOL indique toutefois que le travail est loin d’être terminé: plusieurs milliers d’images restent encore à traiter et pourraient conduire à de nouvelles correspondances. L’opération Shams II illustre ainsi l’utilisation croissante des outils numériques et biométriques dans la traque internationale des réseaux terroristes. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article 126 terroristes identifiés grâce à l’Intelligence artificielle est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Natacha Rey, qui enquêtait sur l'identité sexuelle de Brigitte Macron, est décédée
items.description: La journaliste francaise Natacha Rey, qui avait lance une enquete sur l'identite sexuelle de Brigitte Macron, l'epouse du president francais, est decedee, a annonce le journaliste Xavier Poussard. « C'est avec une immense tristesse que nous apprenons le deces de Natacha Rey, survenu le 13 septembre a Saintes (Charente-Maritime), des suites d'un cancer », a-t-il ecrit sur X. Ses obseques etaient prevues le 18 septembre au cimetiere de Saint-Palle, a Saintes, dans l'ouest de la France. ❤️🔥C’est avec une immense tristesse que nous apprenons le rappel à Dieu de Natacha Rey, survenu le 13 septembre à Saintes (Charente-Maritime), des suites d’un cancer. À l’origine de l’affaire Brigitte Macron, Natacha Rey sera inhumée aujourd’hui à 16 heures au cimetière… pic.twitter.com/aFpItCDWWq — Xavier Poussard (@XavierPoussard) September 18, 2026 En decembre 2021, quelques mois avant l'election presidentielle francaise, Natacha Rey, qui se presentait comme une journaliste independante, avait declare dans une video publiee sur YouTube qu'elle menait depuis plusieurs annees une enquete sur la premiere dame. Elle affirmait que Brigitte, l'ancienne enseignante de Macron, nee Trogneux, qui a 24 ans de plus que le president, etait en realite nee homme et qu'elle s'appelait Jean-Michel. En septembre 2024, un tribunal de Paris a condamne la journaliste francaise, ainsi qu'Amandine Roy, sur la chaîne YouTube de laquelle Rey s'etait exprimee, a des amendes de 13 500 euros pour diffamation. Cependant, en juillet 2025, la cour d'appel de Paris a acquitte Rey dans le proces en diffamation intente contre elle par Brigitte Macron et son frere. La cour a notamment estime que la plupart de ses propos ne remplissaient pas les criteres juridiques de la diffamation. L'avocat de Brigitte Macron a ensuite annonce qu'il ferait appel de cette decision devant la cour de cassation. Le 13 septembre 2026, jour du deces de Natacha Rey, son avocat Francois Danglehant a annonce que sa cliente avait « definitivement » gagne la procedure en diffamation engagee contre elle.

items.title: Tchaoudjo : L’ONG Dimension humaine équipe neuf groupements féminins à Sokodé
items.description: Sokodé, 18 sept. (ATOP) – Neuf groupements de femmes de trois cantons de la commune Tchaoudjo 1, engagés dans la transformation, ont bénéficié d’équipements, le mercredi 16 septembre à Sokodé, en vue de renforcer leur autonomisation économique. Le don est composé de 10 bassines, 7 marmites, 8 plateaux, 26 plateaux d’œufs, 6 mangeoires des poules, 14 seaux, 2 foyers (gente). Il comprend aussi 1 tonneau de 200 litres, 1 couveuse, 1 moulin, 1 déshydrateur pour 10 plateaux et 1 mixeur, batteuse électronique. Ces matériels ont été acquis selon les besoins exprimés par les femmes. Les groupements bénéficiaires proviennent des cantons de Sokodé, de Kpangalam et de Kadambara. M. Yerima remettant symboliquement le don à un groupement Estimé à 3.450.000FCFA, ces équipements ont été mis à disposition de 300 femmes des neuf groupements par l’ONG Dimension humaine (DH) dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de son projet « Résilience et autonomisation des femmes et des jeunes filles pour la lutte contre les Violences basées sur le genre (VBG) dans la commune Tchaoudjo 1 ». Ce projet de six mois, s’intègre dans son programme de promotion de l’autonomisation des femmes et des jeunes. Il bénéficie de l’appui financier de l’Association féminine de solidarité internationale (Equipop) à travers le programme « Femme, paix et sécurité » (FPS). Le président du conseil d’administration de l’ONG DH, Daro Ouro-Akondo a souhaité que cet accompagnement puisse contribuer à créer des moyens de subsistance plus durables et à renforcer la résilience des femmes et jeunes filles bénéficiaires. Le 1 er adjoint au maire de Tchaoudjo 1, Yérima Agrégna a salué l’ONG DH et ses partenaires pour l’exécution de ce projet qui vient appuyer les initiatives du gouvernement et celles de la municipalité pour le bonheur des femmes. Il a demandé aux bénéficiaires d’utiliser judicieusement les équipements reçus en vue de l’atteinte des objectifs. La porte-parole des groupements, Mme Kpelafia Samizétou a indiqué que ce soutien les aidera à produire davantage pour gagner plus d’argent afin de mieux prendre soin de leurs familles. « Nous comptons utiliser les équipements avec responsabilité pour leur durabilité. Nous disons un sincère merci aux donateurs », a-t-elle ajouté. Le chef du canton de Kadambara, Médjéssiribi Madanoun et les représentants des chefs des deux autres cantons ont assisté à la remise des équipements. ATOP/JAE/MEK/BA

items.title: Mahama orders immediate dissolution of National Cathedral Board of Trustees
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has directed the immediate dissolution of the Board of Trustees of the National Cathedral of Ghana project, bringing the board’s role in overseeing the stalled project to an end. The decision was communicated in a letter dated September 18, 2026, and signed by the Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga. The letter, addressed to the Chairman and members of the Board, said, “His Excellency the President has directed the dissolution of the Board of Trustees of the National Cathedral of Ghana Project with immediate effect.” Following the dissolution, the trustees have been directed to liaise with the project consultant and formally hand over the National Cathedral project site to the Ministry by October 31, 2026. Read also: Christians can build National Cathedral if each contributes GH¢1,000 – Mahama The Ministry said the handover was necessary “to allow government to determine the future of the project.” The letter was addressed to the board chaired by Apostle Prof Opoku Onyinah, with copies sent to the Secretary to the President, Chief of Staff at the Jubilee House, the Deputy Minister and Chief Director of the Ministry, as well as the Executive Director of the National Cathedral of Ghana Secretariat. Read also: Taxpayers’ money shouldn’t fund National Cathedral; Christians can contribute towards it – Mahama On behalf of President Mahama, Mr Ayariga expressed appreciation to the trustee members for their service, saying, “I wish to thank you for your commitment to promoting the Christian faith in the country.” The government is now expected to determine the next steps for the National Cathedral project following the formal handover of the site.

items.title: CRC recommendations: Dr Asah-Asante calls for early preparation of gov’t team, rejects five-year term
items.description: Political scientist at the University of Ghana, Dr. Kwame Asah-Asante, has called on political parties to begin preparing to form their governments while still in opposition, dismissing the case for extending Ghana’s presidential term. According to him, political parties determined to establish their governments within the shortest possible time must identify and select the people who will make up their government before assuming office. Dr. Asah-Asante made the remarks on Joy Prime’s Prime Morning on Friday, September 18, while discussing the proposal to extend Ghana’s presidential term from four to five years. He explained that parties should not wait until they are in government before selecting individuals to occupy key positions. “If you are minded and want to have your government in place within the shortest possible time, you can do it. You don’t do it when you are in government; you select the people who will make up your government while you are in opposition,” he said. His comments come after the New Patriotic Party (NPP) rejected the Constitutional Review Committee’s (CRC) recommendation to extend both presidential and parliamentary terms to five years. The CRC, chaired by Prof. H. Kwasi Prempeh, argued that the current four-year cycle leaves governments with limited time to settle in, implement policies, and prepare for the next election. The government, through Attorney-General Dr. Dominic Ayine, has accepted the proposal, saying it will allow more time for policy formulation and assessment. However, Dr. Asah-Asante and the NPP maintain that the four-year mandate promotes regular accountability and that the challenges of transition should be addressed through efficiency and early preparation, rather than an extended tenure.

items.title: Mbappe ends Nike partnership to join Swiss brand On
items.description: France captain Kylian Mbappe has signed with Swiss sportswear brand On, ending a long association with Nike that stretched back to the start of his career, the company announced on Friday. “Today, Swiss sportswear brand On announces its entry into football alongside football champion Kylian Mbappe, marking the beginning of the brand’s journey into the world’s biggest sport,” read a company statement. On also announced that 1998 World Cup winner Thierry Henry had been appointed its football director. The company plans to launch its first football boots next year. “From the beginning, what drew me to On was the opportunity to build something entirely new together that will help shape tomorrow’s game,” said Mbappe. “I want to bring my experience and perspective into what we create, push what’s possible through innovation, and always stay true to the joy of football. “We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning.” On, which is making a major move into the football market with the signing of Mbappe, did not disclose the value of his contract. Founded in 2010 and previously focused on running and tennis footwear, On counts tennis great Roger Federer among its shareholders. Federer also left Nike towards the end of his playing career to join the Zurich-based company. Mbappe’s departure is a blow to Nike, the world’s largest sportswear company, which had been involved with the Real Madrid forward since 2006 and made him one of the leading faces of its football business. The 2018 World Cup winner and all-time leading scorer in the tournament’s history with 22 goals had gradually emerged as Nike’s foremost football ambassador, succeeding Portuguese great Cristiano Ronaldo, who at 41 is approaching the end of his playing career. His exit follows that of Lamine Yamal, a recent World Cup winner with Spain, who swapped Nike for Adidas in 2024. Nike retains under contract several of football’s biggest stars, including Norway striker Erling Haaland and Brazil forward Vinicius Junior. items.title: My support for SHS students goes beyond kindness; it’s a dream come true – Gideon Boako
items.description: Tano North MP, Dr Gideon Boako, has described his support for more than 2,000 Senior High School entrants in the constituency as more than an act of kindness, saying the initiative represents a personal dream shaped by his own difficult childhood. Dr Boako said poverty and a lack of resources nearly prevented him from pursuing Senior High School education, an experience he believes has strengthened his resolve to help young people facing similar challenges. Reflecting on his journey from Bomaa to Bechem Presbyterian Senior High School, he said the support he received from family members and others who intervened in his life, coupled with what he described as God’s grace, enabled him to overcome the difficulties and pursue his ambitions. “What happened yesterday in Tano North was not just an act of kindness. It was a long-held dream come true,” Dr Boako said in a Facebook post on Friday, September 18. He said the educational items presented to the students, including chop boxes, exercise books, school bags and calculators, were his way of giving back to the next generation in multiples of the support he received when he was growing up. “What I did yesterday, by the grace of God, was to give back to my younger brothers and sisters in multiples of what others did for me years ago,” he said. Dr Boako expressed hope that the beneficiaries would overcome their own challenges, realise their dreams and eventually become a source of support to others. He also urged them to remain focused on their education and make Tano North proud.

items.title: President Mahama declares war on filth, says “Ghana must be clean again”
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has launched the National Emergency Waste Evacuation Exercise as part of efforts to tackle Ghana’s sanitation challenges and rid major cities of accumulated waste. The exercise was launched on Friday, September 18, at the IRECOP Centre at Agbogbloshie, where a large refuse heap has become a longstanding sanitation concern. Speaking at the launch, President Mahama described the situation as a national emergency, stressing the need for urgent action to protect public health and restore the dignity of communities affected by poor sanitation. “For too long, we have lived with this shame in the middle of our capital. Today, we say enough is enough. Accra must breathe again. Jamestown must live again.” He said the exercise forms part of his administration’s efforts to deliver on its Clean Ghana Agenda, with the government relying on existing state resources to address the sanitation crisis. Government deploys DRIP equipment President Mahama commended the Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy, and Religious Affairs for adopting what he described as a cost-effective approach by deploying equipment under the District Road Improvement Programme (DRIP) rather than awarding new contracts. “This is the reset we promised. Using what we already have, with our own men and women, our own military, our own assemblies, to solve our own problems. That is value for money. That is self-reliance.” He also commended the Ghana Armed Forces for supporting the exercise with personnel and logistics. The President further acknowledged the Minister for Roads and Highways for securing more than 200 trucks from road contractors to support the waste evacuation exercise. He also praised the Ministry of Finance for agreeing to finance the fuel and maintenance of the DRIP equipment through the District Assemblies Common Fund.

items.title: Tourism Federation woos diaspora investors to Ghana
items.description: The Ghana Tourism Federation (GHATOF) has intensified efforts to position tourism as a major vehicle for attracting investment from the Ghanaian diaspora, particularly African Americans seeking business opportunities and stronger ties with the country. The federation has deliberately brought together diaspora investors, government agencies and private-sector players to provide potential investors with the information and contacts required to make sound investment decisions. The President of GHATOF, Seth Okran, explained that its aim was to go beyond promoting the country as a destination for sightseeing and leisure to using tourism as a gateway to investment in agriculture, real estate, affordable housing, hospitality and other sectors of the economy. He was speaking at a professional business and cultural summit organised by GHATOF in collaboration with a United States business delegation coordinated by a non-governmental organisation (NGO) SHE International Empowerment Global Summit, which focuses on empowering women. The US delegation was led by Dr Cheryl Polote Williamson, who was recently appointed Tourism Ambassador for Diaspora Affairs and also installed as the Developmental Queenmother of Abura Odunase with the stool name Nana Aba Kukua Soma I. Diaspora investment Dr Williamson said the delegation was made up of American women interested in exploring opportunities in the country but who needed reliable information on areas such as investment, real estate, citizenship and other aspects of relocating or doing business in the country. She said the enthusiasm shown by participants indicated that there was significant appetite among members of the diaspora to invest in the country if they were provided with credible information and appropriate institutional support. She said some members had begun following up on some of the opportunities discussed during the workshop, particularly in agriculture, affordable housing, real estate and financial investments, while others had expressed interest in acquiring Ghanaian citizenship. She expressed optimism that the delegation would take immediate steps to explore investment opportunities and build partnerships with relevant institutions in the country. Citizenship pathways The Deputy Director for Diaspora Affairs at the Office of the President, Nana Kyere Agyeman, explaining a special pathway available to people of historic African descent who wished to acquire Ghanaian citizenship, said the process was facilitated through an annual petition submitted to the President, who, upon approval, would direct relevant institutions to commence the citizenship process. He said the Diaspora Affairs Office worked with the Ministry for the Interior and other relevant institutions to establish the criteria and subsequently invite applicants for vetting. He said the current processing fee was GH¢25,000, adding that applicants were required to demonstrate their connection to the country, including their visits to the country for a cumulative period of at least 12 months, business or philanthropic activities, property ownership or other forms of contribution. He said applicants were also required to submit police reports from their countries of origin, as well as from Ghana. He said the government was also introducing an orientation component into the citizenship process to ensure that new citizens understood Ghanaian culture, the country’s political system and what it meant to become part of the Ghanaian society. Investment opportunity An Investment Promotion Officer with the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), Cherk Klutse, said foreigners wishing to invest in the country had to register their company with the Office of the Registrar of Companies, visit the GIPA to register there as well, after which they would be led to a sector regulator to invest. He encouraged members of the diaspora to engage directly with the GIPC to obtain information on incentives and regulatory requirements before committing their funds. The Executive Director of the National Commission on Culture (NCC), Wakefield Ackuaku, encouraged visitors to take advantage of the country’s cultural experiences while exercising caution when purchasing traditional art and other cultural products. He said visitors should patronise reputable art houses and insist on receipts for items purchased to help establish their authenticity and provide evidence of transactions.

items.title: UK lists 4 countries with highest number of deportations in last 5 years
items.description: The UK recorded a steady increase in enforced returns after the number of people returned fell sharply during the COVID-19 pandemic, with nationals of five countries accounting for a significant share of returns in recent years. According to the UK Home Office’s immigration statistics, there were 9,914 enforced returns in the year ending December 2025, representing a 21% increase from the 8,169 recorded in the previous year. The Home Office’s data tracks the five most common nationalitie s for enforced returns from the year ending December 2021 to the year ending December 2025. Here are the four countries whose nationals featured most prominently in the latest figures. 1. Albania Albanian nationals have consistently been the most common nationality for enforced returns over the last five years, according to the Home Office. In the year ending December 2025, 2,440 Albanian nationals were subject to enforced returns, accounting for about 25% of all 9,914 enforced returns recorded during the period. However, the figure was 7% lower than the previous year. The Home Office said enforced returns of Albanian nationals increased following the signing of the UK-Albania Joint Communique in December 2022, which came after substantial numbers of Albanian nationals arrived in the UK by small boats in 2022. Foreign national offenders also accounted for more than half of Albanian enforced returns in the latest year. 2. Romania Romanian nationals recorded the second-highest number of enforced returns among the nationalities highlighted by the Home Office. There were 1,818 enforced returns of Romanian nationals in the year ending December 2025. This represented a 20% increase compared with the previous year. The Home Office said foreign national offenders accounted for more than half of Romanian enforced returns during the latest 12-month period. Romania’s position in the figures comes amid wider changes to the UK’s immigration system following the end of EU free movement. 3. Brazil Brazilian nationals recorded 939 enforced returns from the UK in the year ending December 2025. The figure was 61% higher than the previous year, making Brazil one of the nationalities with the largest increases among the prominent nationalities. Unlike the figures for Albania and Romania, foreign national offenders accounted for a much smaller proportion of Brazilian enforced returns. Brazilian nationals have also featured prominently in the UK’s wider return figures. The Home Office recorded 4,759 voluntary returns of Brazilian nationals in the year ending December 2025. 4. India The number of Indian nationals subject to enforced returns almost doubled to 781 in the year ending December 2025. India was therefore among the nationalities that recorded a particularly sharp increase in enforced returns during the period. The Home Office said, as with Brazil, foreign national offenders accounted for a much smaller proportion of Indian enforced returns than they did for Albanian and Romanian nationals. Indian nationals also recorded a much larger number of voluntary returns, with 8,652 Indians voluntarily returning from the UK during the same 12-month period. items.title: Éducation financière : L’ACAPS lance "Mon cahier de l’assurance"
items.description: L’Autorité de Contrôle des Assurances et de la Prévoyance Sociale (ACAPS) a annoncé, jeudi, le lancement de « Mon cahier de l’assurance », une nouvelle collection pédagogique visant à faciliter la compréhension des notions essentielles de l’assurance. Disponible en arabe et en français, le premier numéro est destiné aux jeunes âgés de 15 à 25 ans, fait savoir l'ACAPS sur son site web. Cette publication est réalisée dans le cadre de la coopération entre l’Autorité et la Banque de France en matière d’éducation financière, formalisée par la convention signée le 17 novembre 2025, précise la même source. Conçu dans une approche pédagogique et ludique, ce premier numéro aborde l’assurance à travers des situations concrètes, des jeux, des quiz et des exercices. Il permet notamment de se familiariser avec les principales notions liées au contrat d’assurance, aux garanties, à la franchise, à l’indemnisation et à la responsabilité, et de mieux comprendre les droits et obligations de l’assuré. Ce premier numéro inaugure une collection structurée par tranches d’âge. D’autres éditions, destinées aux 26-40 ans puis aux plus de 40 ans, viendront progressivement enrichir la collection, avec des contenus adaptés aux différents publics. La publication de « Mon cahier de l’assurance » s’inscrit dans le programme d’éducation financière de l’ACAPS, qui vise notamment à renforcer les connaissances du public en matière d’assurance et à améliorer la compréhension des droits et obligations des assurés, souligne le communiqué. The post Éducation financière : L’ACAPS lance "Mon cahier de l’assurance" appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Gideon Boako supports 2,200 Tano North BECE graduates with SHS essentials
items.description: More than 2,000 Senior High School entrants in the Tano North Constituency have received educational supplies from their Member of Parliament, Dr Gideon Boako, as part of an initiative to support young people beginning their secondary education. The beneficiaries received items including chop boxes, exercise books, school bags and calculators to assist them as they transition from basic education to Senior High School. Dr Boako said the initiative was motivated by his desire to give back to young people in the constituency after receiving support himself during his formative years. He described the intervention as a long-held dream that had finally been realised. “My prayer is that the good Lord who blesses the little to make it bigger for generations will bless these young ones to realize their dreams and become a blessing to others,” he said. The Tano North MP also expressed appreciation to former Second Lady, Samira Bawumia, for attending the event and supporting the initiative, saying her presence helped put smiles on the faces of the beneficiaries. He further thanked traditional leaders, clergy and other dignitaries who attended the programme, while urging the students to take their education seriously and strive to make the constituency proud. “To our dear students: May these items support you as you begin this exciting new chapter. Keep learning, dream big, and make Tano North proud!” he added.

items.title: L’ONG ACDI assiste ses bénéficiaires dans cinq écoles de Haho
items.description: Notsè, 17 sept. (ATOP) – L’ONG Alliance chrétienne pour le développement intégral (ACDI) a offert, le mercredi 16 septembre, des fournitures scolaires à ses bénéficiaires des EPP Asrama, Kponou, Atsitsohoé, Amakpapé, Kpélé et dans les communes Haho1 et 2. Au total 100 kits composés de cahiers, règles, ensembles géométries, de sacs et ses accessoires ont été distribués. Le don permettra de donner de la joie aux enfants bénéficiaires, de soutenir les familles et d’encourager la culture de l’excellence en milieu scolaire. Les bénéficiaires de Kpélé posant avec les membres ACDI Le coordonnateur régional Plateaux-Maritime de l’ONG, Félix Amouzou a relevé la nécessité pour son organisation de prendre en charge l’assistance alimentaire, financière et éducative des bénéficiaires. Il a souligné que l’éducation des enfants consiste à leur assurer l’épanouissement scolaire. M. Amouzou a invité les parents à accompagner la vision de l’ACDI en veillant au bien-être des jeunes garçons et filles. Le directeur de l’EPP Kpéle groupe A et C, Todji Kenouvi Kokouvi a encouragé les parents à visiter l’école afin de mieux appréhender l’environnement d’étude des enfants. Selon lui, l’éducation des jeunes nécessite une collaboration étroite entre parents-enseignants-élève. Elle augmente, dit-il le niveau de surveillance et accroît la compréhension des apprenants. Créée en 2005, l’ACDI œuvre à travers de multiples projets pour sensibiliser les bénéficiaires sur la santé, la vie éducative et les activités génératrices de revenus. ATOP/YM/BA

items.title: 51 personnes poursuivies pour Viol et pédophilie
items.description: Cinq informations judiciaires ouvertes entre mars et juillet 2026 à Dakar concernent au total 51 personnes, poursuivies pour des faits allant notamment du viol et de la pédophilie à la transmission volontaire du VIH/Sida et à la mise en danger de la vie d’autrui, selon le parquet. Le dossier judiciaire prend de l’ampleur à Dakar. Dans un communiqué publié le jeudi 17 septembre 2026, le Procureur de la République près le Tribunal de Grande Instance hors classe de Dakar fait état de cinq informations judiciaires ouvertes entre mars et juillet 2026. Ces procédures, confiées aux juges des Premier et Quatrième cabinet d’instruction, concernent au total 51 personnes. Parmi elles, 49 sont actuellement placées en détention provisoire, tandis que deux bénéficient d’un contrôle judiciaire. Selon le ministère public, 14 personnes ont déjà été renvoyées devant la Chambre criminelle. Dix-neuf autres ont, pour leur part, été orientées vers la Chambre correctionnelle. Les deux dernières procédures, qui concernent 18 personnes, demeurent en cours d’instruction. Leur issue dépend donc encore des investigations menées par les cabinets compétents. Les faits visés par ces différentes procédures sont qualifiés notamment de viol, pédophilie, détournement de mineurs, actes contre nature avec un individu du même sexe, transmission volontaire du VIH/Sida et mise en danger de la vie d’autrui, précise le parquet. À travers ce point de situation, le ministère public fait ainsi le bilan de cinq procédures judiciaires engagées au cours des derniers mois à Dakar, dont certaines ont déjà franchi l’étape de l’instruction tandis que d’autres restent en cours d’examen. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article 51 personnes poursuivies pour Viol et pédophilie est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Burkina Faso : La première promotion de l’École de guerre de l’Institut Tiéfo Amoro effectue sa rentrée
items.description: La première promotion de l’École de guerre de l’Institut de l’enseignement militaire supérieur Tiéfo Amoro (IEMS-TA) a effectué sa rentrée académique ce 17 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Composée de 15 officiers auditeurs, cette première promotion suivra une formation intensive de plus de 11 mois, jusqu’au mois d'août 2027. L'objectif est de renforcer les capacités des cadres militaires dans les domaines de la stratégie, de la planification et de la conduite des opérations. Pour le Commandant de l’IEMS-TA, le Colonel-major Céleste Joseph Moussa Coulibaly, cette rentrée marque une nouvelle étape dans la construction de l’enseignement militaire supérieur au Burkina Faso. Après le lancement des activités de l’Institut en septembre 2025 et la mise en place de l’enseignement militaire supérieur de premier degré, l’ouverture de l’École de guerre porte la formation au niveau stratégique. Le Colonel-major Céleste Joseph Moussa Coulibaly a salué les efforts ayant permis de mettre en place cette formation et l’accompagnement des autorités militaires et universitaires. Il a notamment expliqué que l’École de guerre doit permettre de développer une pensée militaire adaptée aux réalités nationales. « Depuis que cette mission sacrée nous a été confiée, notre mot d'ordre a été très clair : aller vite et aller très vite » , a-t-il déclaré. L’Institut s’appuie également sur une collaboration avec le monde universitaire pour renforcer la dimension académique de la formation. Le Commandant a indiqué que des enseignants et des spécialistes des universités ont participé à la conception du programme destiné aux futurs officiers stratèges. « Le Burkina Faso doit être capable de produire sa propre pensée stratégique et militaire »-©Faso7 Le Chef d'État-Major Général des Armées (CEMGA), le Général de division Moussa Diallo a pour sa part, insisté sur la nécessité pour le Burkina Faso de développer ses propres capacités de réflexion dans le domaine de la défense. « Dans le domaine militaire, la souveraineté implique une exigence, celle de disposer d'un cadre capable de forger le produit de la défense nationale à partir de notre propre environnement stratégique. C'est pourquoi le Burkina Faso doit être capable de produire sa propre pensée stratégique et militaire » , a-t-il déclaré. Pour le CEMGA, l’École de guerre ne doit pas être uniquement un établissement de formation militaire. Elle doit également devenir un espace de réflexion et de confrontation des idées, où l’expérience opérationnelle est mise en relation avec la recherche et l’analyse stratégique. « L'école de guerre que nous ouvrons aujourd'hui doit être un lieu de formation, mais également un lieu de réflexion, un lieu d'enseignement, mais aussi de confrontation des idées, un lieu où l'expérience opérationnelle rencontrera la recherche, un lieu où les leçons tirées du terrain nourriront la réflexion stratégique » , a-t-il soutenu. La formation doit également dépasser le seul cadre militaire. Selon le Général de division Moussa Diallo, les transformations de la guerre imposent désormais aux cadres de la défense de comprendre les dimensions politiques, économiques, diplomatiques et sociales de la puissance nationale. Des officiers appelés à penser et à décider-©Faso7 Aux 15 auditeurs de la première promotion, le CEMGA a demandé une implication particulière dans cette première expérience de l’École de guerre. « Vous ne serez pas seulement des bénéficiaires d'une formation, vous serez, d'une certaine manière, les premiers acteurs de la construction d'une institution appelée à jouer un rôle majeur dans l'avenir de nos Forces armées nationales » , a-t-il déclaré. Il a également insisté sur les exigences intellectuelles auxquelles les auditeurs seront confrontés. Ils devront notamment apprendre à analyser des situations complexes, à remettre en cause certaines certitudes et à distinguer l’information de la connaissance. « Le chef doit savoir réfléchir, mais il doit également savoir décider. Il doit savoir écouter, mais il doit également savoir trancher. Il doit savoir analyser les conséquences de son action, mais il doit également assumer ses responsabilités » , a martelé le Général de division Moussa Diallo. Le Colonel-major Céleste Joseph Moussa Coulibaly a, de son côté, fixé aux auditeurs l’objectif de devenir des officiers capables d’analyser des environnements complexes, de concevoir des plans au niveau stratégique et opérationnel et de conseiller les autorités à l’échelle politico-stratégique. « Notre pays n'a pas seulement besoin d'officiers, qui se contentent seulement de connaître leur métier, mais d'une génération qui pense et comprend la guerre. Nous n'avons pas seulement besoin d'officiers capables de commander des hommes, mais d'officiers capables de commander dans la complexité » , a-t-il affirmé. Le gouvernement promet son accompagnement-©Faso7 Le Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a présenté l’ouverture de cette première promotion comme une nouvelle étape dans l’opérationnalisation de l’IEMS-TA. Il a notamment insisté sur la volonté de former désormais au Burkina Faso les cadres militaires appelés à exercer des responsabilités stratégiques. « On ne peut parler de souveraineté en matière de défense et de sécurité tant que nous allons continuer à envoyer notre élite militaire en formation ailleurs » , a déclaré le Chef du Gouvernement. Selon lui, l’ouverture de l’École de guerre montre que le Burkina Faso dispose désormais de capacités pour assurer localement la formation de son élite militaire jusqu’au niveau stratégique. « Cela montre désormais que le Burkina Faso dispose de toutes les capacités pour former son élite militaire à toutes les échelles, jusqu'au niveau stratégique, afin de disposer évidemment des cadres militaires supérieurs capables de penser, capables de concevoir, capables de conduire les opérations suivant une approche doctrinale endogène, inspirée de notre propre expérience, inspirée de nos traditions, inspirée de notre histoire » , a-t-il ajouté. Le Premier ministre a également assuré que le Gouvernement accompagnera l’Institut dans son développement et la mise à disposition des moyens nécessaires à ses ambitions. L’IEMS-TA, créé en septembre 2025, abrite notamment l’École de guerre, chargée de l’enseignement militaire supérieur de second degré, et l’École d’état-major, chargée du premier degré. La première promotion de l’École de guerre devra désormais achever son parcours académique avant de mettre ses acquis au service des Forces armées nationales. Josué TIENDREBEOGO Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : La première promotion de l’École de guerre de l’Institut Tiéfo Amoro effectue sa rentrée est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.description: Le Camarade Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a présidé, ce vendredi 18 septembre 2026, à Ouagadougou, la cérémonie officielle d’ouverture de l’École de guerre de l’Institut de l’enseignement militaire supérieur Tiéfo Amoro (IEMS-TA). Cette ouverture marque une étape importante dans la formation des cadres supérieurs des Forces armées nationales et l’affirmation de la souveraineté du Burkina Faso en matière de défense et de sécurité. Dans un contexte national et sous-régional marqué par des défis sécuritaires complexes, l’ambition du Chef suprême des Armées, à travers la création de cet institut, est de former des cadres militaires capables de concevoir des réponses adaptées aux réalités du Burkina Faso, en s’appuyant sur une pensée stratégique endogène. L’École de guerre de l’IEMS-TA ouvre ainsi officiellement ses portes à une première promotion composée d'une dizaine d'auditeurs, tous burkinabè. Ils y développeront des compétences approfondies en matière de planification, de commandement, de conduite des opérations et d’analyse stratégique. Pour le Chef du Gouvernement, l'ouverture de l'École de guerre constitue une avancée majeure dans la concrétisation de la vision du Camarade Président du Faso, Chef suprême des Armées, en faveur de la reconquête totale de la souveraineté nationale. Le lancement de la première promotion de cette École de guerre, a-t-il expliqué, traduit la volonté du Burkina Faso de se doter des capacités nécessaires pour former son élite militaire jusqu’au niveau stratégique. Il s’agit de disposer de cadres capables de penser, de concevoir et de conduire les opérations selon « une approche doctrinale endogène inspirée de notre propre expérience, de nos traditions et de notre histoire ». « On ne peut parler de souveraineté en matière de défense et de sécurité tant que nous allons continuer à envoyer notre élite militaire en formation ailleurs », a-t-il souligné. Saluant les progrès accomplis en un an, le Premier ministre a rappelé l’ambition de faire de l’IEMS-TA une référence à l’échelle sous-régionale, africaine et internationale. Après avoir félicité la hiérarchie militaire, le Chef du Gouvernement l’a invitée à poursuivre l’opérationnalisation de l’Institut, tout en réaffirmant le soutien du Gouvernement à la réalisation de ses ambitions. « Je rassure l’ensemble des acteurs que le Gouvernement est engagé à leurs côtés pour mettre à la disposition de cette école les moyens à la hauteur de ses ambitions. Je souhaite plein succès aux auditeurs de cette première promotion », a-t-il déclaré. De son côté, le chef d’état-major général des Armées, le général de division Moussa Diallo, a souligné qu’une nation soucieuse d’assurer durablement sa sécurité doit être capable de penser elle-même sa défense, d’analyser son environnement stratégique et de concevoir des réponses adaptées à ses propres réalités. S’adressant aux auditeurs de la première promotion, il les a appelés à s’engager pleinement dans une formation dont les exigences vont au-delà de la seule acquisition de connaissances. « L’École de guerre attend de vous davantage que l’accumulation de connaissances. Elle attend de vous une transformation intellectuelle et professionnelle. Elle doit contribuer à faire de chacun d’entre vous un officier capable de comprendre, anticiper, concevoir, planifier, décider, conduire, influencer et produire de la pensée utile », a-t-il affirmé. Avec l’ouverture de l’École de guerre, l’IEMS-TA franchit une nouvelle étape dans le développement de la formation militaire supérieure au Burkina Faso. Au-delà de la formation des officiers, l’ouverture de cette École de guerre s’inscrit dans la construction d’une capacité nationale à anticiper les menaces, à définir les choix stratégiques, à conduire la protection des populations et à assurer la préservation de la souveraineté du Burkina Faso. DCRP/Primature

items.title: Hitler Could Have Been Stopped
items.description: Does history repeat itself, or merely rhyme? The historian Timothy W. Ryback has thought about this question a lot. Ryback, the director of the Institute for Historical Justice and Reconciliation at The Hague, has written extensively about Adolf Hitler’s Germany, including in books such as Hitler’s Private Library: The Books That Shaped His Life and Hitler’s First Victims: The Quest for Justice . Ryback’s new book, 53 Days: How Hitler Dismantled a Democracy , which grew out of a series of articles he wrote for The Atlantic , is a straightforward narrative of the period from Monday, January 30, 1933, when Hitler was appointed chancellor, to Thursday, March 23, 1933, when the Reichstag legislative body passed the so-called Enabling Act, which effectively gave the chancellor the power to dissolve the democratic Weimar Republic and inaugurate the Third Reich. As Joseph Goebbels noted at the time, “The big joke on democracy is that it gives its mortal enemies the means of its own destruction.” Ryback’s 53 Days makes no reference to contemporary politics. And yet certain echoes of the 1930s resonate so loudly that it is impossible not to hear them. To cite just a few: Hitler was obsessed with tariffs. Hitler tried to fire his central banker. Hitler was preoccupied with seizing Greenland. Hitler was intent on adding an expensive new wing to the Reich chancellery, part of his grandiose architectural ambitions for the nation’s capital. He attacked and muzzled the press, attempted to purge the civil service of anyone disloyal to him, had a genius for inflaming the populist grievances of his base, and spurred angry young men to take paramilitary action against perceived enemies. [ Read: What the press got wrong about Hitler ] Reductio ad Hitlerum can have the baleful effect of trivializing the Holocaust, which thankfully has no parallel in the modern American context. Yet closely examining Hitler’s rise can yield useful insights into today’s autocratic moment—and help deepen our understanding of history’s unfolding. In a conversation I had with Ryback yesterday at The Atlantic Festival, the historian discussed the rhymes and contingencies of history, the uses and misuses of the past, the lessons of 1933, and what a reexamination of Hitler’s rise can teach us about human agency and fate. This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity. Scott Stossel: Why this book now? Timothy W. Ryback: Histories are written for the era. We read about the things that have meaning for us. Read all the great biographies of Adolf Hitler: You’re not going to find a mention of Hitler’s central banker or his tariff policy. But suddenly, these things matter. For me, the most striking are the resonances in the personality type, the positioning. Hitler’s key to success was to never admit defeat, always double down. We’re used to seeing the newsreel footage of Hitler as the raving lunatic, frothing at the mouth. Well, he despised democracy, but he understood it as well as anyone. When Hitler got 37 percent of the vote in the July 1932 election, that was his high-water mark in terms of a completely open, free election. And he said he should be controlling the country. Listen to his logic: 37 percent is 75 percent of 51 percent, meaning the relative majority of the absolute majority. He used that to incredible effect in co-opting, coddling, or crushing his political allies on the far right before he ever turned to the left. And he was always preaching to his base. I mean, his political advisers would come and say, Whoa, cool it with the anti-Semitism . And Hitler would hear nothing of it. He used that formula, that understanding of democratic processes, to get where he got. Stossel: It has been reported by Trump’s first wife that he kept Mein Kampf by the side of his bed. He denied that and then said No, it was a gift, and it was a collection of Hitler’s speeches . To what extent do you think that Trump is actually looking at Hitler and other fascist leaders of the past for a kind of guidebook for how to take power? And how much of it is just a kind of temperamental instinct for identifying grievances, inflaming them and saying, I will be your solution ? [ Read: The Jews who voted for Hitler ] Ryback: This issue of grievance politics was the essence of Hitler’s political posture. And there were a lot of grievances out there. There was the Treaty of Versailles, which forced Germany to accept full responsibility for all the destruction of the First World War. There were massive reparation payments, which strained the economy. The other thing: He gridlocked the legislative processes time and again. He basically paralyzed the Reichstag, made it impossible for any laws to be passed, forcing the government to rule by executive decree, then turned around and said, Look, democracy doesn’t work as a system. Give me a chance. So I think the modalities were very similar. Keep in mind, the grievances that Hitler was playing off of, actually, a lot of it was legitimate. Stossel: As it is today. You have a chapter in this book titled “Guardrails,” speaking to Hitler’s transgression of guardrails. How do you see, today, the pushing against and possible weakening of guardrails? Ryback: Historians always look back, which lends these processes a sense of historical inevitability, rather than the reality, which is political contingency—what happens from one moment to the next. And I think in that regard, you begin to see Hitler in a very different context. His first day as chancellor, he wants to rewrite election laws. Turns out that’s too complicated. He then wants to ban the Communist Party. There’s pushback: Do we really have a right to do this? Could it cause social unrest? He said, Well, look, if there’s social unrest, we’ll just call in the army. To which the minister of defense, Werner von Blomberg, stands up and says, Mr. Chancellor, with all due respect, our military is trained to defend the German nation against foreign enemies; it is unthinkable that a German soldier could be ordered to shoot on German citizens in German streets. And this puts Hitler in his place. Hitler realized he’s banged up against about every constitutional guardrail there is. The next day, he issues this official memo to the members of the Nazi Party, and he declares war on his own government. Stossel: I’m immediately put in mind of Jim Mattis and Mark Milley , and other folks who, in the first term, said, We are here to defend the Constitution, not to execute your will if it’s not in defense of the Constitution. You anticipated my next question, which was: When you look back at historical events, the natural inclination of both historians and lay people is to understand the narrative as kind of predetermined. But with Hitler’s rise to power, there are so many points along the way where a single action could have stopped him. President Hindenburg had already replaced three chancellors before Hitler came to power. He didn’t have to approve Hitler’s press for the Enabling Act. Do you think that Hitler’s rise and the Third Reich and the Holocaust were inevitable? Ryback: Was the Holocaust inevitable? Big question. Simple answer: no. Look, we’ve got an election coming up in November. You watch Fox News, you get one version of what’s going to happen; watch CNN, The New York Times , you get another. We have no idea yet. One day after the election, you’re going to have every political pundit explaining how this outcome was inevitable. Hitler was going to rallies and saying, I don’t care what the outcome of the election is going to be. I am here to save the German nation. I will not leave the chancellorship. The newspapers at the time said, You know, Mr. Hitler should read the constitution because it’s not up to him to decide whether he stays in office. It’s the president. In some ways, I felt like the book should have been, “How Hitler almost failed to dismantle a democracy.” Forgotten heroes stood up to him: the journalists who were calling him out at every step; the Social Democrats, who were being threatened, and yet pursuing an attempt to save the republic. [ Read: Hitler used a bogus crisis of ‘public order’ to make himself dictator ] Stossel: One key moment in the rise of Hitler and his consolidation of power was obviously the Reichstag fire . Your book comes out before our next election, where we think about October surprises. What worries you, looking ahead to the midterms? Ryback: This is where there are a lot of resonances with the electoral processes at that time. You had a monolithic right-wing movement. You had a fractured left-wing coalition that was continuing to fragment. You had a center group of undecided voters that was going to tip the election in one direction or another. Stossel: When Hitler came to power, I think it’s fair to say that people did not expect that the National Socialists would have been able to win as many of the Reichstag seats as they did. In 2016, everyone thought Hillary was going to win. She did not. In 2024, again, it looked for a long time like Trump’s defeat was inevitable. It was not. Looking ahead to two months from now, polling suggests favorable signals for the Democrats. How do you think about November 2026? Ryback: Hitler said a lot of horrific things. But to my mind, one of the most chilling was when Hitler finally got to power. He said, For the last 12 years, people have been mocking and ridiculing me. No one’s laughing anymore. Hitler did run against Hindenburg in the spring of 1932 for the presidency of Weimar. He lost by 6 million votes. Well, what did he do? He went to court to sue to have the election results overturned amid claims of voter fraud and irregularities by state officials. Where have we heard that before? The judge threw him out on his ear. In March 1933, the German people went to the polls again. It was a referendum on the Hitler administration. No one knew what was going to happen. The Germans saw everything that Hitler had shown the German people, what he wanted the country to be. It was the largest electoral turnout in the history of parliamentary elections in Germany, going back to the 1870s. And they gave Hitler an overwhelming victory. What I would say is: Don’t look at March 5, 1933. Look at April 2026, when the Hungarians had to go to the polls. Viktor Orbán had been in power for 15 years. Orbán had compromised the courts, he had suppressed the opposition press, he had driven the Central European University out of the country—and a lot of dissidents left. And yet, two-thirds of Hungarians voted to get him out of office, and did. Had the German people voted in March 1933 the way the Hungarians voted last spring, there would not have been a Third Reich. There would not have been a Holocaust. And Hitler would have been out of office within weeks.

items.title: Kintinian : un corps sans vie d’une femme découvert dans une mine artisanale à Bouré Kamatiguia
items.description: Le corps sans vie d’une femme âgée de 40 ans a été découvert sur un site d’orpaillage artisanal, à Bouré Kamatiguia, un district relevant de la préfecture de Kintinian. Selon le constat initial dressé par les autorités sécuritaires locales, une consommation excessive de substances excitantes est fortement suspectée. La victime a été formellement identifiée comme étant Maceline Tolno, âgée de 40 ans. Veuve et mère de cinq (5) enfants, elle était originaire de Fermessadou, dans la préfecture de Guéckédou. Comme de nombreux citoyens, elle s’était installée dans cette riche région aurifère pour y mener des activités commerciales de fortune. C’est au cœur d’une zone minière artisanale que la macabre découverte a été faite en début de matinée. Maceline Tolno avait pour habitude de fréquenter ces mines pour y écouler diverses marchandises. Le chef de poste de la localité s’est immédiatement rendu sur les lieux pour procéder aux premières constatations de terrain. D’après ses observations, la victime présentait une quantité notable de morve au niveau de la bouche. Ce signe clinique, souvent lié à une détresse respiratoire aiguë, laisse présumer qu’elle aurait ingéré une dose fatale d’excitants. De sources locales, la quadragénaire vendait de l’alcool fort ainsi que des produits pharmaceutiques hautement prohibés sur les sites miniers, notamment du Tramadol. La présence du corps dans la mine artisanale a rapidement alerté les autorités locales. Les agents de la gendarmerie territoriale de Kintinian se sont déployés sur place pour sécuriser la zone, consigner les éléments matériels et entamer les procédures d’usage. Une enquête officielle a été ouverte pour faire toute la lumière sur les circonstances exactes de sa mort. Ce drame relance inévitablement le débat sur les risques liés à la vente libre et à la consommation abusive de Tramadol et d’alcool frelaté, des substances qui continuent de circuler de manière inquiétante au sein des communautés d’orpailleurs dans la préfecture de Bouré-Kintinian. Mamoudou Kéïta, correspondant à Kintinian 628 61 88 90 L’article Kintinian : un corps sans vie d’une femme découvert dans une mine artisanale à Bouré Kamatiguia est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Burkina/AES-Gestion-affaires-religieuses-Coopération
items.description: Burkina/AES-Gestion-affaires-religieuses-Coopération Burkina/Gestion des affaires religieuses : le Mali veut s’inspirer de l’expérience burkinabè Ouagadougou, 18 sept. 2026 (AIB) – Le ministre malien des Affaires religieuses, du Culte et des Coutumes, Mahamadou Koné, a effectué vendredi une visite de travail à Ouagadougou pour échanger avec les autorités burkinabè et s’inspirer de leur expérience en matière de gestion des affaires religieuses et coutumières, dans la perspective d’un rapprochement des pratiques au sein de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES). « Nous avons voulu que cette visite soit un socle, une base de démarrage dans le cadre de la complémentarité religieuse pour nos peuples », a déclaré Mahamadou Koné, à l’issue des échanges. Selon le ministre malien, cette visite vise notamment à permettre aux deux pays de partager leurs expériences sur la gestion des questions religieuses, du culte et des croyances traditionnelles. « Nos collaborateurs vont se réunir techniquement, ils vont échanger entre techniciens. Une fois abouti à quelque chose de commun, rien n’est impossible pour qu’un jour nous uniformisions nos pratiques et nos manières de gérer nos domaines », a-t-il expliqué. Mahamadou Koné a cité notamment la gestion du Hadj et des pèlerinages chrétiens parmi les domaines susceptibles de faire l’objet d’échanges d’expériences entre les deux pays. La coopération pourrait également concerner la prévention de l’extrémisme violent et la lutte contre le terrorisme, deux problématiques auxquelles sont confrontés le Burkina Faso et le Mali. « Nous aussi, nous luttons contre l’extrémisme violent et le terrorisme. Vous aussi vous luttez contre l’extrémisme violent et le terrorisme. Par quelle manière, avec quel point, quelle stratégie, quelle technique ? », a-t-il déclaré, soulignant l’intérêt de confronter les approches des deux pays. Le ministre malien a par ailleurs indiqué que les croyances traditionnelles seront prises en compte dans les discussions, tout en distinguant celles-ci des religions révélées que sont, selon lui, le christianisme et l’islam. Mahamadou Koné a également exprimé son intérêt pour certaines expériences burkinabè en matière de gestion des affaires religieuses, notamment les textes récemment adoptés sur la liberté religieuse. « Tout récemment, vous avez bien vu comment votre ministre a géré la liberté religieuse et où il y a eu un texte dans ce cadre-là. On va quand même s’inspirer de tout cela pour voir par quelle voie il est sorti, par quelle technique il a fait et par quelle stratégie et quel plan », a-t-il indiqué. Il a toutefois présenté cette démarche comme un processus d’apprentissage mutuel, le Burkina Faso pouvant également tirer profit de l’expérience malienne en matière de gestion des cultes et des croyances traditionnelles. « Toujours dans l’échange, le fruit tombe toujours », a conclu le ministre malien. Agence d’information du Burkina VAT/yos

items.title: At least 26 killed, 82 injured in Sudan-South Sudan border violence
items.description: At least 26 people were killed and 82 injured in deadly violence at the Amiet Common Market in the Abyei region on the border between Sudan and South Sudan, prompting strong condemnation from the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA). According to the recent UNISFA press release , the violence erupted on 15 September after the separate killings of a Ngok Dinka man and a Misseriya man heightened tensions between the two communities . UNISFA said it immediately reinforced its presence around the market, deployed additional troops and began engaging community leaders to prevent further violence and retaliation. “We are actively engaging with the leaders of the two communities who have reiterated their commitment to dialogue and a peaceful resolution to the hostilities,” UNISFA head Lieutenant General Ganesh Kumar Shreshta said. “On the ground, we are taking all measures to protect civilians and prevent retaliation. Our priority is to prevent further loss of life,” he added. The UN mission urged community leaders to pursue dialogue and called on local authorities to work with UNISFA on a swift investigation and to hold those responsible accountable. UNISFA said it would maintain an enhanced security presence in Amiet while continuing efforts to restore calm. Tandjouaré : Du football et des prestations culturelles pour renforcer la cohésion sociale
items.description: Tandjouaré, 17 sept. (ATOP) – Des matches de football masculin et féminin et des prestations culturelles en faveur de la cohésion sociale se sont déroulés le mercredi 16 septembre à Tandjouaré. Ces activités sont organisées par l’ONG « Alafia » dans le cadre du projet « Participation active des filles et femmes à la vie publique, politique et sociale de leurs communautés pour la cohésion sociale, la prévention des conflits et la consolidation de la paix au Togo ». L’objectif est de renforcer la cohésion sociale et la promotion de l’égalité genre dans la préfecture. La danse komposiègue des femmes de Boulogou Les matches se sont joués entre des équipes formées spontanément pour l’occasion. D’une part des jeunes coiffeuses et couturières et d’autre part, des jeunes garçons de la localité, toutes ethnies confondues. Ces rencontres jouées dans un esprit de fraternité, de fair-play et de vivre-ensemble se sont soldées par un score nul et vierge de zéro but partout. Les prestations de danses culturelles, ont quant à elles, permis de mettre en valeur le riche potentiel culturel local. La population a vibré au rythme des danses traditionnel du terroir, notamment le « Talkoudg », le « Komposiègue », le « Bambate » et la danse des boubous traditionnels, exécutés par les femmes de Tandjouaré, de Dodani et de Boulogou. Les femmes peuhles ont également offert une prestation de la danse « Hiro foulbé ». A la fin de la journée, les quatre équipes de football sont reparties avec un trophée, des ballons, des médailles, des T-shirts et des enveloppes. Le maire de Tandjouaré 1, Nam Pakindame a salué le recours aux activités sportives et culturelles comme moyen de rapprochement des communautés. Il a souligné l’importance de renforcer la cohésion sociale pour faire front à l’ennemi et combattre l’extrémisme violent. M. Nam a invité les participants à partager le message reçu et à signaler tout fait suspect aux Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), afin que la cohésion sociale, la paix, le vivre-ensemble et la solidarité règnent au sein de la communauté. La directrice exécutive de l’ONG « Alafia », Mme Tatey Adzoavi Nyuito a relevé que les différences d’origines, de genre et de générations constituent une richesse pour la communauté. Pour elle, ces différences ne devraient pas être des éléments de division, mais au contraire une richesse à exploiter pour le développement de la localité, de la région et du pays. ATOP/SYI/JK/BA

items.title: AFCON 2027Q: Ronald Donkor receives maiden Black Stars call-up for Cote d’Ivoire, Gambia and Morocco games
items.description: Black Stars head coach Carlos Queiroz has handed a maiden call-up to New York Red Bulls’ Ronald Donkor ahead of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers. Ghana is set to face Côte d’Ivoire and Gambia in the opening two games of the AFCON qualifiers before taking on Morocco in Tangier in an international friendly. Queiroz named a 24-man squad for the three games, with the 21-year-old being included in the list for the extended international break. The maiden call-up comes following an impressive outing for the central midfielder for Red Bulls, which has seen him directly involved in six goals. Donkor has two goals and four assists across all competitions for the club this season. Beyond maintaining an 85% pass accuracy and creating 35 chances, the youngster has been a pillar in the middle of the park for his side. His relentless work rate in midfield made him a key force in moving the ball forward. The midfielder moved to America in July 2022, having represented JMG Bamako in the early part of his career. He started with Red Bulls’ junior side before eventually breaking into the first team midway through last season. This season, he has made 23 appearances in MLS, starting in all of them while averaging 83 minutes per game. Donkor has also made two appearances in the US Open Cup.

items.title: Techiman South MP calls for release of remanded Salomey Bafoh Awiti
items.description: Member of Parliament for Techiman South, Martin Adjei-Mensah Korsah, has called on the state to release his constituent, Salomey Bafoh Awiti, following her arrest and remand by the Adentan Circuit Court. Mr Korsah said Ms Awiti was arrested and detained on the night of Sunday, September 13, 2026, describing the circumstances surrounding her arrest, detention and subsequent court appearance as “surprising and disheartening”. He said the family had also received changing explanations from state intelligence agencies about the reason for her arrest. “Even more troubling is the fact that the reason for her arrest as told the family by the State Intelligence Agencies, kept changing until what she was finally charged with in court yesterday,” he said. The Techiman South MP expressed concern that the case could create fear among citizens seeking to exercise their constitutional right to free speech and expression. He described the situation as part of what he called “worrying efforts at cowing citizens into fear in the exercise of their democratic rights to free speech and expression.” Mr Korsah also drew attention to the impact of Ms Awiti’s detention on her family, particularly her young children. “It is both regrettable and condemnable, how a mother could be removed and kept in custody, away from her young children in the fashion being witnessed,” he stated, before appealing to the state to release her and allow her to return to her family. He concluded: “God bless our homeland Ghana and help us to resist oppressors rule!”
